behavior: Ordinary integer and pointer loads accept a proven 64-bit RAX address through the existing typed load action.

RAX-to-RCX address staging precedes accumulator preparation; the same staging helper serves stores. Both compatibility paths and physical write planning agree, with no new machine instruction or register-allocation policy.
Live and dying pointers, a live RCX stride address, caller-clobbering helper calls, exact 8/16/32/64-bit loads and pointer-valued loads preserve values and transaction rollback.
Seven permanent functions pass direct/release routes in three modes with protected page ends, skipped null-slot branches, 56-byte stride loops, input/output guards and independent C checks.
The retained loop and branch reproducers now emit objects. Width/class and read-only-load restrictions remain closed; staging conflicts reject before mutation.
known_boundaries: Read-only specialized loads, i128 aliases and unsupported pointer widths/classes keep their existing admission rules. No floating, aggregate or broader ABI capability is added.
Live scratch values still require a valid preservation home. An unframed fixed-scratch comparison can reject before the new load path; its fixture-development attempts are retained.

Fibonacci now reaches composed-block-binary-imm-rhs at urem i64 by 4096. A small control-flow reproducer has the same rejection and compiles with Clang. Narrower call ABIs and whole-program execution remain later work.
